title: BIG5-CHAT: Shaping LLM Personalities Through Training on Human-Grounded Data

paper.authors: Wenkai Li, Jiarui Liu, Andy Liu, Xuhui Zhou, Mona Diab, Maarten Sap (CMU LTI)
paper.repo: https://github.com/jiarui-liu/Big5Chat (announced in footnote 1 as 'our dataset and code')
paper.repo_commit: NONE - the repository is empty. `git clone --depth 1` returned 'You appear to have cloned an empty repository' and `git ls-remote` returns no refs; the GitHub API reports size 0 KB, created_at and pushed_at both 2024-10-20T22:25:30Z, license null. Nothing was ever pushed.
paper.other_artifacts: The dataset - not linked from the paper - is on Hugging Face as wenkai-li/big5_chat (apache-2.0, last modified 2024-11-18, one file big5_chat_dataset.csv, size category 10K-100K, 155 downloads). No SFT/DPO LoRA adapters, no evaluation code, no personality-test item files, no model outputs are published anywhere; the author's 25 public HF models are unrelated earlier work.

dependence.note: The paper's contribution is training (SFT and DPO on LLaMA-3-8B/70B over 100k human-grounded dialogues), which is outside the inference-only scope. Commercial models appear only as baselines: GPT-4o-mini as an alternative data generator (Table 1) and GPT-4o / GPT-4o-mini as prompting baselines on the BFI and IPIP-NEO personality tests (Table 12). The paper's own headline claim (training beats prompting) is therefore not re-executable by inference alone.

claim.statement: Prompting a proprietary model is not a substitute for training on BIG5-CHAT: under instruction-based prompting (Prompt-Inst), GPT-4o reaches an average BFI score of 4.9 (high) / 1.5 (low) and IPIP-NEO 4.7 (high) / 1.8 (low), i.e. saturated, unrealistically extreme trait expression rather than the human-like distributions the SFT/DPO models produce (Table 12, Appendix; Section 'Necessity of dataset construction').
claim.metric: Mean self-report score (1-5 Likert) on the 44-item BFI and the 120-item IPIP-NEO, reported per trait at induced High and Low levels and as a High/Low average over the five traits; standard deviation over 5 repeated runs.
claim.original_source: Paper Table 12 (Appendix, full personality test results; 'BFI GPT-4o' and 'IPIP-NEO GPT-4o' blocks) and Table 1 (data-generation baselines). Values are one decimal with a one-decimal standard deviation over 5 runs.

protocol.prompt_source: Paper Appendix D.5 only. Prompt-Inst system prompt is quoted in full as 'You are a person with {level} {trait}.'; Prompt-Demo prepends 'Here are 10 examples of how people like you have responded in different situations...' plus 10 fixed in-context examples drawn from BIG5-CHAT. The questionnaire-administration wrapper (how each of the 44/120 items is presented and how the 1-5 answer is parsed) is NOT given.

params.source: Section 'Evaluation procedure': 'We measured the standard deviation by repeating each experiment five times, using a temperature setting of 0.6.'

protocol.evaluation: Mean Likert score per trait, computed from the BFI (44 items, John et al. 1999, administration following Huang et al. 2024) and IPIP-NEO-120 (Johnson 2014, administration following Jiang et al. 2024a). Reverse-keying and trait aggregation are standard for both instruments but the paper ships no scoring script.

artifacts.notes: Dataset yes, pipeline no. The announced repository is empty, so prompts, questionnaire administration, scoring, the SFT/DPO training scripts, the trained adapters and every model output are unavailable. Only the four prompt fragments quoted in Appendix D.2/D.5 exist.

blockers: The announced code repository https://github.com/jiarui-liu/Big5Chat is empty (0 KB, no commits, no licence) - no prompts beyond four appendix fragments, no questionnaire administration or scoring code, no released outputs.
No dated snapshot: 'GPT-4o' is an undated alias and the experiment window (arXiv v1 2024-10-21) straddles the 2024-10-02 cutover, so the arm may well have been gpt-4o-2024-08-06, which is dead.

Neither the census live_id (gpt-4-turbo, a reference-list artifact) nor the paper's other OpenAI arm (gpt-4o-mini, alias) is on the retirement list, so there is no unambiguous retiring snapshot to anchor a card on.
The paper's contribution is training; the SFT/DPO LoRA adapters are unreleased, so the comparison arm of the claim cannot be re-produced either - only the frozen published numbers can be cited.
Questionnaire administration is underspecified (item-per-call vs whole-instrument-per-call, reverse-keying, answer parsing), and max_tokens is unreported.

budget.assumptions: HYPOTHETICAL, only if the card were unblocked and a proxy accepted. Prompt-Inst rows only: (44 BFI + 120 IPIP-NEO) items x 5 traits x 2 levels x 5 repeats = 8,200 calls, ~150 input tokens per call (short system prompt plus one item), ~5 output tokens. 5 repeats is the paper's own sampling scheme, so the 3-seed default does not apply. Adding the Prompt-Demo rows (10 in-context examples, ~1,500 input tokens) would raise the total to about USD 69. If the instruments are administered whole rather than item-by-item, the call count drops to 500 and the cost to under USD 1.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 (only if unblocked). Primary numbers: the BFI and IPIP-NEO High/Low averages for GPT-4o under Prompt-Inst (4.9/1.5 and 4.7/1.8). Survival = re-run means within the original +/- 1.96 x the reported SD over 5 runs (+/- 0.2) AND the behavioural direction holds: instruction prompting still saturates the scale (High >= 4.5, Low <= 2.0) and still separates further from the human-like distributions than the trained models do. Partial = levels move but the High-Low gap remains above 2.5 points. Death = the model no longer moves with the induced level, or refuses trait role-play.
judgment.notes: The comparison arm (SFT/DPO LLaMA-3-70B) is frozen at its published values because no adapters were released, so only the GPT-4o side can move. Self-report personality inventories are in every model's training data, which limits what a re-run can establish.

user_checks: Accept the empty repository as a hard stop, or reconstruct the questionnaire administration ourselves from the two appendix prompt fragments plus the public BFI-44 / IPIP-NEO-120 item sets (which would be our pipeline, not the authors')?
If reconstructed: accept gpt-4o-2024-05-13 as a proxy for the undated 'GPT-4o' alias although the October 2024 experiment window makes gpt-4o-2024-08-06 (dead) at least as likely?
Is an appendix-table prompting baseline (Table 12) worth a card at all when the paper's headline claim is a training result we do not re-run?
domain_notes: BIG5-CHAT is 100,000 dialogues built by conditioning SODA social scenarios on PsychGenerator-derived Big Five expression, with a RoBERTa-style classifier (93.8% test accuracy) used to verify trait realisation. Training is LoRA SFT and DPO on LLaMA-3-8B/70B-Instruct with GPTQ quantisation on 4 A6000s. The dataset itself is human-grounded, not model-distilled, so the training data poses no distillation problem - the obstacles here are purely the missing pipeline and the unresolvable alias. The reasoning-benchmark half of the paper (SocialIQA, GSM8K, MathQA, TruthfulQA, CommonsenseQA, PIQA, MMLU, GPQA via lm-evaluation-harness) involves no commercial model at all.
